items.summary: The Third Circuit affirmed the District Court's denial of Holy Trinity Ukrainian Catholic Church's preliminary injunction in its lawsuit against Township of Collier regarding denial of a rezoning application for a shrine project. Although the court found Holy Trinity likely to succeed on the merits of its Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act and Free Exercise Clause claims, it held that preliminary relief was not necessary because relief could be obtained at final judgment and temporary disruption of the status quo was not warranted.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–123: To require the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology and the Administrator of National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to develop a standard methodology for identifying the country of origin of
items.summary: Public Law 119–123, also known as the “Illegal Red Snapper and Tuna Enforcement Act,” requires the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology and the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to develop a standard methodology. This methodology, based on chemical analysis, is for identifying the country of origin of seafood to support enforcement against illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing and seafood fraud. The law mandates pilot studies on red snapper and tuna and requires a report on the methodology and its operational plan to be submitted to Congress within two years.
items.title: Public Law 119–123: To require the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology and the Administrator of National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to develop a standard methodology for identifying the country of origin of seafood to support enforcement against illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–124: To amend the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 to provide a clear definition of adequate consideration for certain closely held stock, and for other purposes. Public Law 124 Public Law 119–124 140 Stat. 107
items.summary: Public Law 119–124, titled the “Retire through Ownership Act,” amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). It specifies that a fiduciary of an employee stock ownership plan may rely in good faith on an independent valuation expert's assessment of adequate consideration for closely held stock, provided the expert uses principles from IRS Revenue Ruling 59–60. The law clarifies that this amendment does not expand the Secretary's regulatory authority or alter fiduciary obligations under section 404 of ERISA.
items.title: Public Law 119–124: To amend the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 to provide a clear definition of adequate consideration for certain closely held stock, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service 9 CFR Part 94 [Docket No. APHIS-2023-0016] RIN 0579-AE83 Minimum Maturation Temperature for Beef and Ovine Meat From Regions Affected With Foot-and-Mouth Disease AGENCY: A
items.summary: We are proposing to amend the regulations regarding the minimum maturation temperature for fresh (chilled or frozen) boneless beef and ovine meat from certain listed regions or countries affected with foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) from 4 °C to 2 °C. All other existing mitigations for the importation of beef from regions or countries affected with FMD would remain unchanged. This action is needed to align the regulations with the World Organization for Animal Health's standards for FMD minimum maturation temperatures, while continuing to protect the United States against the introduction of FMD.
items.title: Minimum Maturation Temperature for Beef and Ovine Meat From Regions Affected With Foot-and-Mouth Disease

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration 50 CFR Part 635 [Docket No. 260813-0186; RTID 0648-XG124] Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Fisheries; Closure of the General Category October Thr
items.summary: NMFS closes the General category fishery for Atlantic bluefin tuna (BFT) for the remainder of the October through November time period. The General category may only retain, possess, or land large medium and giant ( i.e., measuring 73 inches (185 centimeters (cm) curved fork length (CFL) or greater) BFT when the fishery is open. This action also waives the previously scheduled restricted-fishing days (RFDs) for the remainder of the October through November time period. With the RFDs waived during the closure, fishermen aboard General category permitted vessels and HMS Charter/Headboat permitted vessels may tag and release BFT of all sizes, subject to the requirements of the catch-and-release and tag-and-release programs. On December 1, 2026, the fishery will reopen automatically.
items.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Bluefin Tuna Fisheries; Closure of the General Category October Through November Fishery for 2026
